Miguel — thanks for the level of specificity, that helps. I want to propose a path forward that balances Biocorp's need for tangible protection with Redwood's enterprise risk controls. Key points of our compromise proposal: 

1) Severity ladder and credits: maintain per-incident credits per SLA for single isolated incidents. For repeated incidents we will escalate credit multipliers (e.g., 1x credit for first S1, 2x for second S1 within 90 days).

2) Termination right: we can agree to a termination-for-cause right after three S1 events in a rolling 90-day window, provided Redwood has a 14-day cure period and that termination is subject to mutual exit assistance terms (data export, runbook handover).

3) Fee-at-risk / capped cash remedy: Redwood cannot accept an uncapped liquidated-damages regime. We can accept an escrow-style arrangement but limited to one month of committed recurring fees held in escrow (or a bookkeeping hold) that is releasable upon confirmed breaches. Finance and legal will need to include standard carve-outs (force majeure, scheduled maintenance, customer-side misconfiguration).

4) Liability cap and transition assistance: cap aggregate remedy for SLA-related cash draws at 3x monthly committed fees in any 12-month period; as a commercial concession Redwood will include one month of onboarding credit if Biocorp executes a 24-month committed agreement.

5) Governance: any draw from escrow requires an independent post-incident review within 30 days; dispute escalation path to an SLA panel (1 rep from each side + neutral expert).

This structure preserves the ability to terminate while limiting Redwood's potential cash exposure and introducing an independent review to avoid misclassification of incidents. If Biocorp prefers larger escrow amounts, we can price that into the commitment (higher monthly fee in exchange for larger fee-at-risk).

Please let me know if this addresses your core asks or if Legal wants redlineable language we can route through our counsel. I'm happy to capture this in a short term sheet for your CFO/legal. We can also put a DocuSign placeholder if you want quick visibility into economics.

— Rishi Malhotra
Head of Commercials, Redwood Inference
